page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with no margin notes. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Below the text: a catchword and a gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: hoc Epiphonema: Ἀνσχοῦ γὰρ ἐμφύοντα πέτρας καὶ κρημνῶν περιέχοντα, βασιλεῖ δὲ πίστεως καὶ χάριτος τῷ ἰσχυροτέρῳ ἢ δὲ ὀχυρώτερον. ταῦτά σοι τὸ ἡρωτιμὸν ἀνοίγει πέλαγος, ταῦτα τὴν Πελοπόννησον[?]. Latrones rupes & saxa incolunt, ac praecipitijs se tuentur: Regi autem nihil fide & beneuolentia firmius aut munitius esse potest. Haec tibi mare Creticum & Peloponnesum aperiet.
Testatur autem omnium temporum historia, munitarum arcium & urbium fiduciam, tam principibus quàm subiectis, saepenumerò plurimùm obfuisse. Exiftimò autè inter alias eius mali causas, has esse.
i. Quòd verè eiusmodi arces, sudore, sumtibus & sanguine pauperum extruuntur.
iuxta illud: Nam lapides è muris clamabũt; & ligna è structuris ligneis respondebũt illis. Væ aedificanti urbe sanguine, & ei qui stabilit ciuitatem iniquitate, Abac.2.11.12.
2. Quòd fiducia munitionum fascinati tā principes, quàm populi, saepe mouent bella non necessaria: quae alioquin intermissuri erant: & dant poenas fiduciae temeritatisque suae.
3. Quòd vbi hostes ea loca occupárunt praesidijsq; impositis firmárunt, non facile inde exturbari possint.
4. Quòd iusto Dei iudicio id in scandalū

page.notes: Greek passage is in a small, dense typeface; the Greek transcription is my best reading and several words are doubtful (the passage near "ἀνσχοῦ", "ἡρωτιμὸν" and the last Greek phrase) and should be checked against the scan. Lines 1 to 2 of the Greek are italic in appearance but I have not marked them as italic. The paragraph beginning "4." continues onto the next page. The mark "b &" at the foot is read as signature "b" and catchword "&c". A small ornament appears at the foot centre and was left out as not printed text.
